headline: High-risk write and network overlap: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while transformers can write and exfiltrate outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported app content, while transformers can process files and emit text that may be copied back into ChatGPT. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path, though no shared MCP or automatic bridge is documented. The interaction is pair-specific and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF outputs from transformers are pasted or opened in ChatGPT Desktop without sanitization
IF ChatGPT Desktop is granted access to files or screenshots containing attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste boundary and strip instructions from B outputs
Open B-generated files in a plain-text viewer before sending to A
Disable clipboard bridging during review sessions
Mark untrusted documents as data-only in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to B outputs before A ingests them

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and transformers has broad network egress plus file access. If A’s sensitive inputs are forwarded into B, B can transmit them externally; if B writes artifacts back, A may ingest them. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so this is not higher than medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files or screenshots from ChatGPT Desktop are copied into transformers
IF transformers sends processed artifacts to a remote endpoint or hub
mitigations: Keep sensitive A inputs out of B runs
Use local-only datasets for B when handling A-derived content
Review B network destinations before execution
Delete intermediate files after each run
requires-engineering: isolate A and B in separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write files in overlapping workflows: ChatGPT Desktop reads user-uploaded and app files, while transformers can write files and run subprocesses. In default use, concurrent edits or generated artifacts can overwrite each other, and the pair lacks documented locking or coordination. Uncertainty about the shared workspace pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or project tree
IF transformers writes artifacts while ChatGPT Desktop is reading or summarizing the same files
mitigations: Use separate output directories for A and B
Serialize file edits with a manual lock file
Snapshot the workspace before running B
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can summarize or act on files and screenshots, and transformers can generate text artifacts that A may treat as authoritative. Because B has no built-in verification of A’s interpretation, errors can cascade from B’s outputs into A’s downstream reasoning. The pathway exists in default workflows, but no direct action authority is shown.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop uses transformers output as source material without independent verification
IF B-generated summaries are forwarded into A for user-facing answers
mitigations: Require a second-pass human check on B outputs before A uses them
Ask A to cite original sources, not B summaries
Keep B outputs in a draft-only folder
Compare B claims against raw inputs before reuse
requires-engineering: add automated verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not specify regulated-data handling, residency, or retention mismatches. ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files and screenshots, while transformers handles local files and broad data types, but no explicit compliance conflict is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, though the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents under different retention policies
IF one agent is used in a jurisdictional workflow not covered by the other
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention and deletion expectations
Review vendor terms for residency constraints
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance mapping
